query: If airlines eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints in the reviews, how much would the average Overall Rating improve?

per_column.name: primary_cabin_service_complaint
per_column.rationale: The query explicitly targets eliminating the most common cabin-service complaints; this column identifies that intervenable treatment (an airline can change service to remove a complaint category).

per_column.name: complaint_recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Whether a complaint recurs is downstream of the complaint itself and lies on the path to the rating, not a common cause of treatment and outcome.

per_column.name: service_gap_category
per_column.rationale: This is essentially a re-grouping/abstraction of the complaint type (the treatment), not a distinct common cause; it functions as a treatment recode rather than a confounder.

per_column.name: traveler_segment_susceptibility
per_column.rationale: Traveler segment plausibly affects both which complaints are raised and baseline overall rating, and is not named in the query (though Type of Traveller exists in the original table).

per_column.name: class_quality_gap
per_column.rationale: Service class shapes both the complaints experienced and the overall rating; a class-based quality gap is a common cause not named in the query, though Class is an existing original column.

per_column.name: positive_offset_factor
per_column.rationale: Positive aspects that offset the rating are competing causes of the outcome but not common causes of the complaint treatment; better treated as covariates than confounders.

per_column.name: expectation_gap
per_column.rationale: Prior expectations can drive both the likelihood of registering complaints and the rating given; a plausible unnamed common cause.

per_column.name: service_inconsistency
per_column.rationale: Variability in service delivery is part of the mechanism producing complaints and the rating, sitting on the causal path rather than being an antecedent common cause.

per_column.name: class_of_service_quality_gap
per_column.rationale: A duplicate-style class quality gap indicator; class differences confound complaint incidence and overall rating and are not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The set correctly establishes an intervenable treatment: the most common cabin-service complaint is something an airline can act to eliminate, matching the what-if intent. It also supplies several genuine, unnamed common causes (traveler segment, class-based quality gaps, expectation gap) that would need adjustment to read off the counterfactual rating improvement. However, quality is diluted by (a) redundant treatment recodings (service_gap_category) and near-duplicate class-gap columns, and (b) several columns that are mediators/competing outcome causes (complaint_recurrence_signal, service_inconsistency, positive_offset_factor) rather than confounders. The treatment and a handful of valid confounders are present, but the confounder layer is partly mechanical and overlapping, yielding moderate quality.
